lessons.title: Story Time: A Determined Nurse
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss the significance of overcoming a challenge.
success_criteria: I can say what challenge Mary Seacole faced.
I can say how she overcame it.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what it means to be determined.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a biography extract about Mary Seacole, modelling discussion of the challenges she faced and overcame.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and record a challenge Mary Seacole faced and how she overcame it.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of a challenge/resolution narrative — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family about Mary Seacole.

lessons.title: Quarter Hour Recap and Application
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply quarter hour time-telling confidently.
success_criteria: I can read quarter past and quarter to times.
I can apply this to a real situation.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap quarter hour times from last week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Consolidate quarter hour time-telling with real-life application (journey times, remedy schedules).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve quarter-hour time problems in a real-life context.
key_questions: What time will it be in a quarter of an hour?

differentiation.support: Use a clock face to work out answers

lessons.assessment_notes: Consolidation check on quarter hour time-telling — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Practise quarter hour times on a clock at home.

lessons.title: Who Was Mary Seacole?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall key facts about Mary Seacole's life.
success_criteria: I can say when Mary Seacole lived.
I can say what she is famous for.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a picture of Mary Seacole.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce Mary Seacole's life and work — travelling to the Crimea and setting up the 'British Hotel' to care for soldiers.
lessons.independent_task: Children record key facts about Mary Seacole in a fact file.
key_questions: What did she do in the Crimea?

differentiation.support: Complete fact file with word bank

lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall of a significant historical individual — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family what you learned about Mary Seacole.

lessons.title: Writing About Mary Seacole
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write factual sentences about Mary Seacole using the past tense.
success_criteria: I can write a fact about Mary Seacole.
I can use the past tense consistently.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about Mary Seacole from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a factual sentence about Mary Seacole using consistent past tense.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 factual sentences about Mary Seacole.
key_questions: Is your sentence in the past tense?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note factual writing with tense consistency — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family a fact about Mary Seacole.

lessons.title: Adding Two-Digit Numbers (Crossing Tens)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to add two-digit numbers where the ones cross a multiple of ten.
success_criteria: I can add two-digit numbers.
I can explain how I crossed the tens boundary.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap adding two-digit numbers from Week 3.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model adding two-digit numbers where the ones total crosses a ten (e.g. 27 + 15), using a number line.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve addition problems crossing the tens boundary using a number line.
key_questions: What happens when the ones make more than 10?
How do you show this on the number line?

differentiation.greater_depth: Solve some mentally, explaining the method

lessons.assessment_notes: Record more complex two-digit addition understanding — evidence for MATHS.N2.

lessons.title: Mary Seacole's Journey
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe Mary Seacole's journey to the Crimea.
success_criteria: I can describe her journey.
I can say why it was difficult.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a simple map showing Jamaica, England and the Crimea.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss Mary Seacole's journey and the obstacles she faced (being turned away, funding her own trip).
lessons.independent_task: Children trace Mary Seacole's journey on a simple map, recording key facts.

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain obstacles and how she overcame them in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note historical/geographical cross-curricular understanding — evidence for HIST.1/GEOG links.
lessons.home_link: Trace a journey on a map with your family.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Seacole-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read words related to Mary Seacole's story.
success_criteria: I can read themed words.
I can read a sentence about Mary Seacole.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to words related to this week's topic (e.g. 'travel', 'brave', 'help').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading this week's themed words.

lessons.title: Subtracting Two-Digit Numbers (Crossing Tens)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to subtract two-digit numbers where the ones cross a multiple of ten.
success_criteria: I can subtract two-digit numbers.
I can explain how I crossed the tens boundary.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap subtracting two-digit numbers from Week 3.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model subtracting two-digit numbers crossing a ten (e.g. 42 - 15), using a number line.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve subtraction problems crossing the tens boundary using a number line.
key_questions: How do you show this on the number line?

differentiation.greater_depth: Solve some mentally, explaining the method

lessons.assessment_notes: Record more complex two-digit subtraction understanding — evidence for MATHS.N2.

lessons.title: How Was Mary Seacole Treated?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss, sensitively and age-appropriately, that Mary Seacole faced unfair treatment.
success_criteria: I can say she was treated unfairly at times.
I can say this was wrong.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Mary Seacole being turned away when she first offered to help.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss, sensitively and age-appropriately, that Mary Seacole faced prejudice, and that despite this she persevered and helped many people.
lessons.independent_task: Children record that Mary Seacole was treated unfairly but persevered, focusing on her achievement.
resources_needed: Age-appropriate resource on Mary Seacole's story
key_questions: Was it fair how she was treated?
What did she do despite this?

differentiation.greater_depth: Discuss why perseverance was so admirable

lessons.assessment_notes: Note age-appropriate historical understanding handled sensitively — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap that everyone deserves fair treatment, and Mary Seacole's perseverance.
lessons.home_link: Talk about treating everyone fairly with your family.

lessons.title: Hot-Seating Mary Seacole
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer questions in role as Mary Seacole.
success_criteria: I can answer a question in role.
I can use facts I've learned.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about Mary Seacole learned this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model hot-seating as Mary Seacole, answering questions using known facts.
lessons.independent_task: Children take turns hot-seating as Mary Seacole, answering classmates' questions.
key_questions: Mary, why did you want to help soldiers?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer unprompted, in character, with detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and factual recall in role — evidence for ENG.SL1/HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Pretend to be Mary Seacole and tell your family about your 'journey'.

lessons.title: Two-Step Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve two-step addition and subtraction word problems.
success_criteria: I can solve a two-step problem.
I can show each step of my working.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving a two-step word problem (e.g. add then subtract), showing each step.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve two-step word problems using a historical context (e.g. supplies for a journey), showing working.

differentiation.support: Solve with adult support, breaking down each step
differentiation.greater_depth: Solve independently and explain both steps

lessons.assessment_notes: Record two-step problem solving, a key Year 2 objective — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a two-step word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Why Is Mary Seacole Remembered?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why Mary Seacole is remembered today.
success_criteria: I can say why she is remembered.
I can name something named after her.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss things named after famous people.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss Mary Seacole's legacy (statue, awards, recognition in nursing history).
lessons.independent_task: Children record why they think Mary Seacole is still remembered today.
key_questions: Why do we still talk about her today?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give detailed reasoning about her lasting impact

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of historical legacy and significance — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Talk about someone your family admires and why.

lessons.title: Mary Seacole Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about Mary Seacole.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about Mary Seacole.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about Mary Seacole, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What did Mary Seacole do in the Crimea?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on Mary Seacole facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Addition, Subtraction, Two-Step Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply addition, subtraction and two-step problem skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can add and subtract crossing tens.
I can solve a two-step problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's addition, subtraction and problem solving.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: addition/subtraction, two-step problems.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 9 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising addition and subtraction over the weekend.

lessons.title: Mary Seacole Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about Mary Seacole's life and legacy.
success_criteria: I can name what Mary Seacole did.
I can say why she is remembered.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about Mary Seacole.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Mary Seacole' display combining fact files, journey maps, and hot-seat notes from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about Mary Seacole?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning, preparing to compare with Florence Nightingale next week — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished Mary Seacole display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about Mary Seacole with your family.
